translations.text: Now today God's Church throughout the whole world celebrates the feast of the blessed children whom the cruel Herod killed in an impious persecution because of Christ's birth, as the gospel narrative clearly tells us.
Matthew wrote in the first book of Christ these words about the time of the Saviour's birth, and said,

"When the Saviour was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod, behold, three astrologers came from the eastern part of the world to the city of Jerusalem, asking thus: Where is the King of the Jewish people, who has been born?
We have truly seen his star in the east, and we have come in order to worship him. Then King Herod, hearing this, was greatly troubled, and all the citizens together with him.
He then gathered all the chief priests and the scribes of the people, and asked where Christ's birthplace would be. They said: in Bethlehem of Judea.

For thus it is written by the prophet Micah: O you Bethlehem, Jewish land, you are by no means the least of cities among the Jewish rulers; out of you shall come the Leader who shall rule and guide the people of Israel.
Then Herod called the three astrologers to a private conference, and eagerly asked them at what time the star had first appeared to them, and sent them to Bethlehem,
saying thus: Go quickly, and inquire about the child, and when you find it, make it known to me, that I may worship him.
The astrologers went on according to the king's speech, and behold, the star which they had seen in the east glided before them, until it stood above the lodging where the child was dwelling.
They saw the star and rejoiced greatly. Then they went in and found the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they worshipped him.
They opened their treasure-chests and offered him gifts: gold, and incense, and myrrh.
Then God warned them in a dream and commanded that they should not return to the cruel King Herod, but should turn away from him by another way, and so they came to their homeland.
Behold, then God's angel appeared to Joseph, the child's foster-father, in dreams, saying: 'Arise, and take this child with the mother,
and flee to the land of Egypt, and stay there until I tell you again; for truly it is coming that Herod will plot how he may destroy the child.'
Joseph then arose by night, and brought the child together with the mother to the land of Egypt, and dwelt there until Herod died;
so that the prophecy might be fulfilled which had earlier spoken thus about that journey: Out of the land of Egypt I have called my son."
Now historians say that meanwhile Herod was accused before the Roman emperor, who at that time ruled the whole world.
Then he went to Rome at the emperor's command, so that he might clear himself, if he could.
Then he cleared himself very cunningly, being so very eloquent that the emperor sent him back to the Jewish kingdom with greater honour.
When he came home, he remembered what he had earlier intended concerning the child, and saw that he had been deceived by the astrologers, and he became greatly enraged.

He then sent his executioners, and slew all the male children who were in the city of Bethlehem and in all its borders, from the child of two years to one of a single night, according to the time which he had learned from the astrologers.

Then was fulfilled the prophecy of Jeremiah, who prophesied thus: "A voice is heard on high, great weeping and wailing: Rachel wept for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not."
On the twelfth day after Christ's birth the three astrologers came to Herod and asked him about the child who had been born;
and when they had learned his birthplace, they went to the child, and would not return to the cruel murderer, as he had commanded.
Then he could not evade the emperor's command, and so, because of his long journey, the slaughter of the children was put off for longer than he had intended;
and they were then gloriously martyred on this present day; not, however, in the year in which Christ was born, but two years later, after the cruel one's return home.
He was not of noble birth, nor did he belong in any way to the royal line; but he came to the royal dignity through plotting and treachery;
just as Moses wrote about it, that the Jewish royal line should not fail until Christ himself came.
Then Christ came at the time when the royal family failed, and the foreigner Herod ruled the kingdom.
Then he became greatly afraid and dreaded that his kingdom would fall through the coming of the true king.
Then he called the astrologers to a private conference, and eagerly asked them at what time they had first seen the star, because he feared, as indeed happened, that they would not come back to him.

Therefore he ordered all the boy-children of the city's district to be killed, from the child of two winters down to the child one night old. He thought that if he killed them all, the one he was seeking would not escape.
But he was unmindful of the holy scripture, which says, "There is no wisdom, nor any counsel, of any avail against God."
The treacherous Herod said to the astrologers, "Go, and inquire diligently about the child, and tell me, so that I too may worship him."
But afterwards he revealed his deceitful plotting, what he would have done if he had found him, when he destroyed all those of his age for the sake of persecuting him alone.
Needlessly he plotted against Christ: he did not come because he wanted to take for himself his earthly kingdom, or that of any other king, by force;

but he came because he wanted to give his heavenly kingdom to faithful people. He did not come in order to be raised up on a splendid royal throne, but in order to be nailed with scorn to the gallows of the cross.
Yet he chose to avoid the cruel one's plotting by flight, not because he was fleeing from death, he who had come to the world of his own will to suffer;
but it would have been too soon if he had been killed then in the cradle, as though his coming would then have been hidden from mankind;
therefore God's angel forestalled the impious one's plan, and commanded the foster-father to carry the heavenly prince quickly out of that land.
Christ did not neglect his young soldiers, though he was not bodily present at their slaughter; but he sent them from this miserable life to his eternal kingdom.
Blessed were they born, that they were allowed to suffer death for his sake. Blessed is their age, which could not yet confess Christ, and was allowed to suffer for Christ.
They were the Savior's witnesses, though they did not yet know him. They were not ripe for slaughter, but they nevertheless blessedly died into life.

Blessed was their birth, because they found eternal life at the very entrance of the present life. They were snatched from their mothers' breasts, but they were immediately entrusted to the bosoms of angels.
The wicked persecutor could not have benefited the little ones so greatly with any service as he benefited them with the hatred of his fierce persecution.
They are called the flowers of the martyrs, because they were like flowers springing up in the midst of the cold of unbelief, withered as it were by the frost of persecution.
Blessed are the wombs that bore them, and the breasts that suckled such ones.
Truly the mothers suffered in their children's martyrdom; the sword that pierced the children's limbs reached the mothers' hearts;
and it must be that they are sharers of the eternal reward, since they were companions in the suffering.
They were killed while small and without understanding, but they will arise at the common judgement with full stature and heavenly wisdom.
We shall all come to one age at the common resurrection, though we now depart from this world at different ages.
The gospel says that Rachel wept for her children and would not be comforted, because they are not.
Rachel was the name of the wife of Jacob the patriarch, and she signified God's Church, which weeps for her spiritual children;

but she will not be comforted in such a way that they should return again to worldly struggle, those who once overcame the world through a victorious death and escaped its miseries, to be crowned with glory with Christ.

Truly the impious Herod did not enjoy his kingdom with long-lasting prosperity, but without delay divine vengeance came upon him, which destroyed him with manifold misery, and also showed in what torments he must suffer eternally after his death.
An unspeakable disease seized him; his body burned outwardly with a lingering fever, and he was likewise all burned up within, and burst apart.
He had a great desire for food, yet he could not satisfy his greed with any amount of eating. He shook with fever, and wheezed dreadfully, and drew anguished sighs, so that he could hardly breathe.
Dropsy overcame him below the girdle, to such an extent that his genitals swarmed with worms, and stinking poison flowed continually from his swollen feet.
Unbearable itching overcame his whole body, and an incredible swelling afflicted his bowels.
A stinking vapour came from his mouth, so that hardly any physician could come near him. He killed many of the physicians, saying that they could heal him and would not.
He was tormented by constant sleeplessness, so that he spent whole wakeful nights without sleep; and if he dozed a little, nightly phantoms at once tormented him, so that sleep became hateful to him.
When he longed intensely for his life, he ordered himself to be carried across the river Jordan, to where there were hot baths, which were said to be healing for sick bodies.
Then it also seemed good to his physicians that they should bathe him in warm oil.
But when he was brought into this bathing, his body went completely limp, so that his eyes turned like those of dying men, and he lay speechless and senseless.
Afterwards, when he came back, he ordered himself to be carried to the city of Jericho.

When he despaired of his life, he summoned to him all the Jewish elders from every city and ordered them to be shut up in prison. And he called to him his sister Salome and her husband Alexander, and said,
"I know that this Jewish people will greatly rejoice at my death; but I can have an honourable funeral, attended by a mourning multitude, if you will obey my commands.
"As soon as I die, kill all these Jewish elders whom I have shut up in prison; then their kinsmen, who would rejoice at my death, will be forced into mourning."
He then appointed his soldiers for the slaughter and ordered each of them to be given fifty shillings as payment, so that they would not hold back their hands from the bloodshed.
When he was tormented with immense anguish, he ordered his own son Antipater to be wickedly killed, in addition to the two whom he had killed before.
At last, when he felt his death approaching, he ordered his knife to be handed to him to pare an apple, and he stabbed himself violently, so that it quivered in him.
Such was the death of Herod, who wickedly plotted against the coming of the heavenly prince, and impiously killed the innocent little children of the same age as him.
Then, after Herod's death, behold, an angel of God appeared to Joseph in a dream in the land of Egypt, saying thus,
"Arise, and take the child and his mother together, and go back to the land of Israel; for truly those who plotted against the child's life are dead."
He then arose, as the angel had commanded him, and brought the child with his mother to the land of Israel.
Then Joseph learned that Archelaus reigned in the land of Judea after his father Herod, and he did not dare to come near him.
Then he was again admonished in a dream that he should turn aside to Galilee, because that region was not so very near to the king, though it was in his kingdom.
The child then lived in the town called Nazareth, so that the prophecy might be fulfilled which said that he would be called a Nazarene.
The angel said to Joseph: "Those who plotted against the child's life are dead."
With that word he showed that more of the Jewish elders had plotted Christ's death; but it befell them very justly that they all perished together with their impious lord.
We will not draw out this story any longer, lest it seem tedious to you; but ask for intercession for yourselves from these innocent martyrs.
They are the ones who follow Christ in white garments wherever he goes; and they stand before his throne without any stain,
having their palm branches in their hands, and they sing the new song of praise in honour of the Almighty, who lives and reigns for ever without end. Amen.
